mainTopic: Snake stories and remedies, and the משנה's rules on medicinal foods and drinks on שבת (מי דקלים, זיתום, כוס עקרין)
overview: This amud continues the גמרא's long list of remedies (רפואות). It opens with the end of a story about an official in פומבדיתא who was bitten by a snake. Every cure failed, and אביי explained that this was a punishment for breaking a rabbinic decree, which has no cure. The גמרא then gives practical advice about snakes: what to do if one wraps around you, chases you, targets a woman, or enters a woman's body. Next it returns to the משנה about healing on שבת. The words 'all foods' and 'all drinks' include unusual foods and drinks taken for healing, but not urine, because people do not normally drink it. The גמרא then explains the משנה's exceptions. מי דקלים is a strong laxative water, and זיתום המצרי is another medicinal brew, with רב יוסף and רב פפא giving different recipes. Finally, רבי יוחנן gives the recipe for כוס עקרין and its uses, and a list of backup remedies begins that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The official bitten by a snake and the failed cure
steps.stepSummary: An official in פומבדיתא was bitten by a snake. The cure needed a white donkey, but every white donkey in town turned out to be a טריפה, and a lion ate the last one.
steps.simpleTranslation: An official of פומבדיתא was bitten by a snake. There were thirteen white donkeys in פומבדיתא. They tore them all open, and every one was found to be a טריפה. There was one more donkey on the far side of פומבדיתא, but before they could bring it, a lion ate it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about a man bitten by a snake whose cure kept failing in strange ways. This story sets up אביי's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the previous amud (109b), the cure for a snakebite was to tear open the fetus of a white female donkey and place it on the bite, as long as it is not a טריפה. Here every possible donkey failed, one after another. A series of failures this unusual hints that something beyond nature is happening.

keyTerms.meaning: An official or appointee (a Jewish town officer)
An animal with a fatal defect

phrases.english: An official of Pumbedita
whom a snake bit,
there were thirteen white donkeys
in Pumbedita,
they tore them all open,
and they were found to be tereifah.
There was one on the other side of Pumbedita,
phrases.notes: One more white donkey, far away.

phrases.english: by the time they went to bring it,
a lion ate it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the snakebite-remedy discussion from the previous amud (109b).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every attempt at the white-donkey cure failed in unusual ways.

steps.title: אביי explains: a snake of the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: אביי suggests the man was bitten by a 'snake of the רבנן' as a punishment, and that kind of bite has no cure. He brings a פסוק as his source.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to them: Perhaps a 'snake of the רבנן' bit him, which has no cure, as it says: 'One who breaks through a fence will be bitten by a snake.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains why every cure failed: the bite was a punishment for breaking a rabbinic rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'fence' (גדר) in the פסוק is read as a rabbinic decree, since the רבנן's rules are fences around the Torah. A bite that comes as a punishment cannot be healed by natural remedies, which explains the chain of failures.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'snake of the Rabbis': a bite that comes as punishment for violating their decree
One who breaks through a fence (here, a rabbinic safeguard)

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains a basic idea about rabbinic decrees: breaking a fence the רבנן set up is treated very seriously.

phrases.english: Abaye said to them:
Perhaps a snake of the Rabbis bit him,
which has no cure,
as it is written: "And one who breaches a fence, a snake will bite him" (Ecclesiastes 10:8).

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ אַבָּיֵי: דִילְמָא חִיוְיָא דְּרַבָּנַן טַרְקֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the strange failures described in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bite that comes as punishment for breaking a rabbinic decree has no natural cure.

steps.title: They confirm: he broke רב יצחק בר ביסנא's decree
steps.stepSummary: The people confirm אביי's guess. After רב died, רב יצחק בר ביסנא banned bringing myrtle and palm branches with bells to weddings, and this official did it anyway. The snake bit him and he died.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Yes, רבי. When רב died, רב יצחק בר ביסנא decreed that no one may bring myrtle and palm branches to a wedding hall with bells. This man went and brought myrtle and palm branches to the wedding hall with bells. A snake bit him, and he died.
steps.whatsHappening: The townspeople supply the fact that proves אביי right: the official had openly broken a rabbinic decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The decree was a sign of mourning for רב, limiting wedding celebrations. Because the official broke it, his case fits the פסוק exactly, and his death confirms that the bite had no cure.

keyTerms.meaning: He passed away (lit. his soul rested)

steps.whatToRemember: The white-donkey cure failed because the bite was a punishment for breaking a rabbinic decree, and such a bite has no cure.

phrases.english: They said to him: Yes, my teacher,
for when Rav died,
Rav Yitzḥak bar Bisna decreed
that no one should bring myrtle and palm branches
to a wedding hall [with bells],
and he went and brought myrtle and palm branches
phrases.notes: "He" is the official who was bitten.

phrases.english: to the wedding hall with bells.
A snake bit him, and he died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms אביי's suggestion with the facts.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that this was a 'snake of the רבנן'
steps.raayaSupportSource: The official had violated רב יצחק בר ביסנא's mourning decree

steps.title: What to do if a snake wraps around you
steps.stepSummary: If a snake coils around a person, he should go into water, put a basket over his head, ease the snake into it, throw it into the water, and then climb out.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a snake wraps itself around someone, he should go down into water, turn a basket over his head, and slowly ease the snake off himself into it. Once the snake climbs into the basket, he should throw it into the water, then climb out and leave.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from the story to practical advice and starts a list of snake-safety instructions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The water makes the snake look for higher, drier ground, so it climbs into the basket. The person can then get rid of the snake without fighting it.

keyTerms.meaning: He should go down into water

phrases.english: One whom a snake encircled —
should go down into water
and turn a basket over his head
and gradually ease it off himself,
and when it climbs onto it (the basket) —
he should throw it into the water
and climb out and come away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the story to a list of practical snake remedies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Use water and a basket to remove a snake that has wrapped around you.

steps.title: Escaping a snake that is pursuing you
steps.stepSummary: A list of escape methods for someone a snake is chasing: ride on a friend, jump a ditch, cross a river, sleep on a raised bed guarded by cats, and run in sand.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a snake is angry at someone and chasing him: if a friend is with him, the friend should carry him four אמות. If not, he should jump over a ditch. If not, he should cross a river. At night he should put his bed on four barrels and sleep outside under the stars. He should bring four cats and tie them to the four legs of the bed, and scatter twigs there, so that when the cats hear the snake moving through them they eat it. Someone being chased should run through sand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues its safety list with ways to escape a snake that is chasing a person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each method breaks the snake's trail: carrying, jumping, or crossing water stops it from following the person's scent. At night, the raised bed and the cats protect him, and the noisy twigs warn the cats. Sand slows a snake down more than it slows a person.

keyTerms.meaning: That is angry at him / pursues him jealously

phrases.english: One at whom a snake is angry (and pursues),
if his friend is with him —
let him carry him four cubits,
and if not — let him jump over a ditch,
and if not — let him cross a river,
and at night — let him place his bed
on four barrels,
and sleep under the stars,
and bring four cats
and tie them to the four legs of his bed,
and bring twigs and throw them there,
so that when they (the cats) hear its sound, they eat it.
One whom it is running after —
should run in sand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another danger case to the list of snake remedies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Escape a pursuing snake by breaking its trail, guarding the bed at night, and running in sand.

steps.title: Testing whether a snake has set its desire on a woman
steps.stepSummary: If a woman sees a snake and is not sure whether it desires her, she throws her garment in front of it. If the snake wraps itself in the garment, it desires her; if not, it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a woman sees a snake and does not know whether it has set its mind on her or not, she should take off her garment and throw it in front of the snake. If the snake wraps itself in it, it has set its mind on her. If not, it has not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a test a woman can use to find out whether a snake is targeting her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The garment carries her scent. A snake that is drawn to her will wrap itself in the clothing, which shows whether she is in danger. This test sets up the next question: what should she do if the answer is yes?

keyTerms.meaning: Has set its mind (desire) on her

phrases.aramaic: הַאי אִיתְּתָא דְּחָזְיָא חִיוְיָא, וְלָא יָדְעָה
phrases.english: A woman whom a snake sees, and she does not know
whether it has set its mind on her
or has not set its mind on her —
she should take off her garment and throw it before it,
if it wraps itself in them,
its mind is on her,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָא — לָא יָהֵיב דַּעְתֵּיהּ עִילָּוַהּ.
phrases.english: and if not — it has not set its mind on her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new danger case: a snake that targets a woman.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Throwing her garment in front of the snake shows whether it desires her.

steps.title: What is her remedy?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the woman should do if the test shows the snake does desire her.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is her remedy?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short follow-up question. This sets up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 only told her how to find out whether she is in danger. Now the גמרא asks how she can get the snake to leave her alone.

phrases.english: What is her remedy?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follow-up question on the case in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can a woman make a snake that desires her leave her alone?

steps.title: First answer: relations in front of the snake
steps.stepSummary: The first answer is that she should have relations with her husband in front of the snake.
steps.simpleTranslation: She should have relations with her husband in front of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a first answer to the question about her remedy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that seeing her with her husband will make the snake lose interest in her. The next step challenges this.

phrases.english: She should have relations (with her husband) in front of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She should have relations with her husband in front of the snake.

steps.title: Some reject this: it would only increase the desire
steps.stepSummary: איכא דאמרי reject the first answer, because that would make the snake's desire even stronger.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: All the more so its desire will grow stronger!
steps.whatsHappening: Another opinion rejects the first remedy and argues that it would backfire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection says the plan would have the opposite effect: watching her would make the snake want her more, not less. Since the first answer is rejected, the next step gives a different remedy.

phrases.english: Some say:
All the more so its desire will overpower it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי: כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן דְּתָקֵיף לֵיהּ יִצְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 8.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It would strengthen the snake's desire instead of ending it.

steps.title: Second answer: hair, nails, and 'I am a נדה'
steps.stepSummary: Instead, she should throw some of her hair and nails at the snake and say, 'I am a נדה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, she should take some of her hair and her nails, throw them at it, and say: 'I am a נדה.'
steps.whatsHappening: Following the rejection, the גמרא gives a different remedy for the woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא shows that this replaces the rejected answer. The idea is to make the snake lose interest by telling it she is unavailable, along with throwing part of her body at it.

phrases.english: Rather, she should take from her hair and her nails
and throw them at it,
and say: "I am a menstruating woman."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the remedy rejected in step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She throws her hair and nails at the snake and says 'I am a נדה.'
steps.whatToRemember: For a woman a snake desires, the first remedy is rejected. The accepted method is throwing hair and nails at it while saying 'I am a נדה.'

steps.title: Drawing out a snake that entered a woman
steps.stepSummary: If a snake has entered a woman's body, they lure it out with the smell of fatty meat roasting and a mix of cress and fragrant wine, grab it with tongs, and burn it so it does not return.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a snake has entered a woman, they should spread her legs and seat her on two barrels. They should bring fatty meat and throw it onto coals, and bring a bowl of cress and fragrant wine, put them there, and mix them together. She should hold tongs in her hand, because when the snake smells the aroma it comes out. Then she should take it and burn it in the fire, because if not, it will come back to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends this section of snake remedies with the most serious case: getting out a snake that has entered a woman's body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The strong smells draw the snake out of her body, and the tongs let her catch it safely. Burning it is required, because otherwise it will return to her.
steps.whatToRemember: The snake section closes with this method: lure the snake out with strong smells, catch it with tongs, and burn it so it cannot return.

phrases.english: A woman whom a snake has entered,
they should spread her legs and seat her on two barrels,
and bring fatty meat
and throw it onto coals,
and bring a bowl of cress
and fragrant wine and place them there,
and mix them together,
and she should hold tongs in her hand,
for when it smells the aroma — it comes out,
and she should take it and burn it in the fire,
for if not — it will return to her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a final, more severe snake case to the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lure the snake out with strong aromas, catch it with tongs, and burn it so it does not return.

steps.title: What does 'all foods' come to include?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'all foods' and asks what extra case the word 'all' adds.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said 'All foods.' What does 'all foods' come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the words of the משנה and asks what the word 'all' adds. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה could have just said 'foods.' The extra word 'all' seems to point to some unusual food that we might have thought is forbidden. The גמרא wants to know which food that is.

keyTerms.meaning: What does it come to include?

phrases.english: [The משנה said:] 'All foods,' etc.
'All foods' — what does it come to include?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the גמרא returns to the משנה after the side discussion about snakes.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which unusual food the word 'all' comes to permit.

steps.title: It includes spleen for teeth and vetch for the intestines
steps.stepSummary: 'All foods' includes spleen eaten for the teeth and vetch eaten for the intestines.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include spleen for the teeth and vetch for the intestines.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'all' includes foods that people eat mainly to heal, like spleen for teeth and vetch for the intestines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are not common foods, and someone eating them is clearly doing it for healing. Even so, since they are still food, they are allowed on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Vetch (a kind of legume, usually animal feed)

phrases.english: To include spleen for the teeth
and vetch for the intestines.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Spleen for the teeth and vetch for the intestines may be eaten on שבת.

steps.title: What does 'all drinks' come to include?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the same question about the משנה's words 'all drinks.'
steps.simpleTranslation: 'All drinks' — what does it come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same kind of question about the משנה's phrase 'all drinks.' The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This uses the same pattern as step 12. The word 'all' should be adding some unusual drink.

phrases.english: 'All drinks' — what does it come to include?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same question as step 12, now asked about drinks.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which unusual drink the word 'all' comes to permit.

steps.title: It includes caper water with vinegar
steps.stepSummary: 'All drinks' includes water in which capers were soaked, mixed with vinegar.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include caper water mixed with vinegar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'all drinks' includes caper water with vinegar, even though people drink it mostly for healing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works just like the foods. An unusual drink that is still a drink may be used for healing on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Water in which capers were soaked

phrases.english: To include caper water with vinegar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Caper water with vinegar may be drunk on שבת.

steps.title: רבינא asks whether one may drink urine on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רבא whether drinking urine as a remedy is allowed on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רבא: What is the law about drinking urine on שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא asks רבא if urine counts as one of the 'drinks' the משנה allows on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the word 'all' includes unusual drinks like caper water, maybe it includes even urine, which was drunk as a remedy. The question is how far the word 'all' stretches.

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rava:
What is the law about drinking urine on Shabbat?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the limits of 'all drinks' from step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether urine counts as a 'drink' that is permitted for healing on שבת.

steps.title: Urine is not a normal drink, so it is not allowed
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers from the משנה: 'all drinks' means things people actually drink, and people do not drink urine.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: We learned, 'He may drink all drinks,' and people do not drink urine.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers that urine is forbidden, because the משנה only allows real drinks, and people do not normally drink urine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's permission covers things that count as normal food or drink. Caper water is a drink, even if unusual. Urine is not a drink at all, so drinking it is plainly a medical act, and that is forbidden on שבת.
steps.whatToRemember: The permission covers anything that counts as normal food or drink, even if it is eaten for healing. Something people never eat or drink normally, like urine, does not count.

phrases.english: He said to him: We have learned:
'He may drink all drinks,'
and people do not drink urine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Urine is forbidden, because it is not something people normally drink.

steps.title: משנה quote: except palm water, with a variant reading 'water that stabs'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes 'except for מי דקלים' and brings a ברייתא that reads 'מי דקרים' instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Except for palm water.' It was taught: 'Except for water that stabs.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's exception, then notes that a ברייתא has a slightly different version of the word. This sets up the explanation of both versions in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two readings differ by only one letter (ל or ר). The גמרא does not pick one yet. It will explain what each version means.

phrases.english: 'Except for palm water.'
It was taught: 'Except for water that stabs.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next phrase in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are two versions of the משנה's exception: מי דקלים and מי דקרים.

steps.title: Explaining both names
steps.stepSummary: 'מי דקרים' means it pierces the gall bladder. 'מי דקלים' means it comes from between two palm trees.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who taught 'water that stabs' means it pierces the gall bladder. The one who said 'palm water' means it comes out from between two palm trees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why each version gets its name. Both names describe the same water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no real argument here. One name describes what the water does: it 'stabs,' meaning it attacks the gall bladder. The other name describes where it comes from: two palm trees.

phrases.english: The one who taught 'water that stabs' —
because they pierce the gall bladder;
and the one who said 'palm water' —
because they come out from two palm trees.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two readings brought in step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both names fit the same water. One names its effect and the other names its source.

steps.title: What exactly is palm water?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a fuller description of מי דקלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is palm water?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a fuller picture of what this palm water is. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing the water 'comes from palm trees' is not enough. The גמרא wants to know what the water is and why it is forbidden.

phrases.english: What is palm water?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for more detail after step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A precise description of מי דקלים.

steps.title: A spring between two palms in ארץ ישראל that acts as a laxative
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר ברונא describes a spring between two palm trees in ארץ ישראל. The first cup loosens the bowels, the second causes diarrhea, and the third passes through unchanged.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר ברונא said: There are two palm trees in the West (ארץ ישראל), and a spring of water comes out from between them. The first cup loosens, the next causes diarrhea, and the next comes out just the way it went in.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר ברונא explains that מי דקלים is water from a special spring that works as a strong laxative.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we see why it is excluded. It is not a normal drink. It is a powerful medicine, so drinking it on שבת is clearly a medical act. The third cup 'comes out as it went in,' because by then the bowels are completely empty.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Beruna said:
There are two palm trees in the West (Eretz Yisrael),
and a spring of water comes out from between them.
The first cup loosens [the bowels];
the next causes diarrhea;

phrases.aramaic: וְאִידַּךְ — כִּי הֵיכִי דְּעָיְילִי הָכִי נָפְקִי.
phrases.english: and the next — just as it goes in, so it comes out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מי דקלים is laxative spring water from between two palms in ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: עולא: Babylonian beer works even better
steps.stepSummary: עולא says that for him, Babylonian beer works better as a laxative than palm water.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: For me, I drink Babylonian beer, and it works better than them.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא, who came from ארץ ישראל, compares the palm water to Babylonian beer and says the beer is more effective.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a side comment on the remedy. Beer is a normal drink, so it would be allowed on שבת, but עולא notes that it also has a strong laxative effect.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
For me, I drink Babylonian beer,
and it is better than them (the palm waters).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a comparison to the palm water described in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Babylonian beer is a stronger laxative than palm water.

steps.title: Only if he was not used to beer for forty days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits עולא's claim: the beer only works this way for someone who has not drunk it regularly for forty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is only if he was not used to it for forty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a condition to עולא's statement: the beer has this strong effect only on someone who has not been drinking it for the last forty days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who drinks beer regularly gets used to it, and it stops working as a remedy. So עולא's claim is true only for someone the beer is new to.

phrases.english: And this is only if he was not used to it
for forty days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits עולא's statement in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The beer works only if he has not been drinking it for forty days.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the recipe for זיתום המצרי
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says זיתום המצרי (identified with 'water that stabs') is made of one-third barley, one-third saffron, and one-third salt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: זיתום המצרי is one-third barley, one-third saffron, and one-third salt.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף describes another strong medicinal drink, Egyptian זיתום, and gives its recipe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As רש״י explains, this identifies the 'מי דקרים' version of the משנה as Egyptian זיתום. Like the palm water, it is a medicine for the bowels, not a normal drink.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Egyptian zitom is one-third barley,
and one-third saffron,
and one-third salt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another identification and a recipe for the forbidden drink.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: זיתום = barley, saffron, and salt in equal parts.

steps.title: רב פפא: a wheat-based version, plus a memory aid
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the recipe uses wheat instead of barley, and puts cumin with the salt. The גמרא gives the memory aid 'סיסאני' to keep the opinions straight.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: one-third wheat, one-third saffron, and one-third salt and cumin. Your memory aid is 'סיסאני.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא disagrees about the recipe, using wheat and adding cumin. The גמרא then gives a memory aid so we remember who said barley.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only differences are wheat instead of barley, and cumin added to the salt. The memory aid 'סיסאני' (with the letter ס) links רב יוסף (who has a ס in his name) to שעורים, barley, spelled with ש, a letter that sounds like ס.

keyTerms.meaning: A word used as a memory aid

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
one-third wheat,
and one-third saffron,
and one-third salt and cumin.
And your memory aid: sisanei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different recipe from רב יוסף's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: זיתום = wheat, saffron, and salt with cumin.

steps.title: When to drink זיתום and how it works
steps.stepSummary: זיתום is drunk between פסח and עצרת. It loosens a blocked person and firms up a loose one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one drinks it between פסח and עצרת. For one who is blocked, it loosens him, and for one who is loose, it blocks him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains when this drink is used and what it does to the bowels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The drink balances the body in both directions. It helps constipation and also helps diarrhea. This shows clearly that it is a medicine and not a normal drink.

phrases.english: And one drinks them between Passover and Shavuot;
one who is blocked — it loosens him;
and one who is loose — it blocks him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Describes the use of the זיתום from steps 24-25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: זיתום is taken between פסח and עצרת and balances the bowels.

steps.title: What is כוס עקרין?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's second exception, כוס עקרין, and asks what it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And כוס עקרין.' What is כוס עקרין?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the משנה's second forbidden drink and asks what it is. The recipe comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the palm water, this drink is excluded from 'all drinks.' The גמרא needs to define it first.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'cup of roots,' a medicinal drink

phrases.english: 'And kos ikarin.'
What is kos ikarin?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next phrase of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the drink כוס עקרין is made of.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's recipe: three ingredients ground together
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן: take a זוז-weight each of Alexandrian gum, alum, and garden saffron, and grind them together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Bring a זוז-weight of Alexandrian gum, a זוז-weight of alum, and a זוז-weight of garden saffron, and grind them together.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the recipe for כוס עקרין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three ingredients are equal in weight. The mixture is a medicine, not a drink people take for pleasure, so it is excluded on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: The weight of a זוז coin

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Let one bring a zuz-weight of Alexandrian gum,
and a zuz-weight of alum,
and a zuz-weight of garden saffron,
and let one grind them together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Gum, alum, and saffron, one זוז-weight each, ground together.

steps.title: Using it for a זבה and for jaundice
steps.stepSummary: For a זבה: three in wine, and she does not become barren. For jaundice: two in beer, and he becomes sterile.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a זבה: three in wine, and she does not become barren. For jaundice: two in beer, and he becomes sterile.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the drink is used for two illnesses and what side effect each use has.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taken with wine, it cures a זבה without making her barren. Taken with beer for jaundice, it does cure the illness, but it also causes sterility.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman with an abnormal flow of blood

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two uses: with wine for a זבה there is NO sterility, while with beer for jaundice there IS sterility.

phrases.english: For a zavah — three in wine,
and she does not become barren.
For jaundice — two in beer,
and he becomes sterile.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the recipe from step 28 is used.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three in wine cures a זבה without sterility. Two in beer cures jaundice but causes sterility.

steps.title: Restating the זבה remedy to lead into backup remedies
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats the זבה remedy and begins: 'If not, let one bring three…', which opens a list of other cures.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a זבה: three in wine, and she does not become barren. And if not, let one bring three…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the זבה remedy to set up a list of backup cures in case it does not work. The list continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This repetition is on purpose. It starts a new section: 'and if this does not help, try the following.' The rest of the sentence comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: And if not (if it did not help)

phrases.english: For a zavah, three in wine,
and she does not become barren.
And if not — let one bring three…
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the זבה line from step 29 for a new purpose: introducing alternative remedies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the first remedy fails, there are other remedies, listed next.
